note: Things to take up rather than attend once — a studio, a choir, a book group, a garden, a table of chess. Hand-researched: every record was checked against the organisation's own page on `lastVerified`, and none of them is sport, which has its own tab. `rhythm` is how often it runs (weekly, monthly, anytime, occasional); `commitment` is what it asks of you to start (dropin, book, term, member); `firstStep` says how to begin in the organisation's own terms. Read by the Regulars tab in js/app.js.

items.title: Lindy in the Park
items.coordsFrom: hand-placed from the description (JFK Drive, 8th to 10th Avenue)
items.times: Every Sunday, 11am to 2pm, with a free beginners’ lesson from 12 to 12.30 — cancelled for rain and Bay to Breakers
items.firstStep: Turn up at noon for the free lesson — no partner needed
items.area: John F. Kennedy Drive between 8th and 10th Avenues, Golden Gate Park
items.why: The longest-running swing dance in the Bay Area, going since 1996 on the car-free stretch of JFK Drive. Every Sunday a speaker comes out, dancers of every age take over the road, and at noon anybody who has never danced gets a free half-hour lesson in which leaders and followers rotate, so you do not need to bring a partner. By the third Sunday you will recognise half the floor.
items.hoursNote: Every Sunday, 11am to 2pm, with a free beginners’ lesson from 12 to 12.30 — cancelled for rain and Bay to Breakers

items.title: Chess at the Mechanics' Institute
items.cadence: Tuesday nights, plus classes and free events
items.times: The Tuesday Night Marathon runs in seasons of weekly rated games; classes and free events through the week
items.firstStep: Join the Institute ($150 a year, $80 for students), then enter the next Tuesday season
items.priceNote: $150 a year · marathon entry $70 for members
items.why: The oldest continuously running chess club in the United States, in a members' library off Market Street. The Tuesday Night Marathon is the club's heartbeat: one rated game a week for a season, often after a lecture by a master, against whoever the pairings give you. It is the rare chess habit that fits after work and that scales from your first rated game upward.
items.hoursNote: The Tuesday Night Marathon runs in seasons of weekly rated games; classes and free events through the week

items.title: Repair Café Palo Alto
items.cadence: A few Sundays a year · next 8 November, 11am–3pm
items.times: Sunday 8 November 2026, 11am to 3pm; check-in closes at 2.30pm
items.firstStep: Bring up to two broken things, or sign up as a fixer
items.area: Museum of American Heritage, 351 Homer Avenue
items.source: Repair Café Palo Alto · Museum of American Heritage
items.why: Volunteer engineers, sewers and tinkerers set up in a museum of old machines and fix whatever the town brings in — lamps, toasters, jeans — while you watch and learn how. It comes round a few times a year, with the odd weeknight session at Rinconada Library. Go once as a customer, and next time consider signing up to fix.
items.hoursNote: Sunday 8 November 2026, 11am to 3pm; check-in closes at 2.30pm

items.title: BATS School of Improv
items.times: Foundation 1 to 6 for adults, in person at Fort Mason and online
items.firstStep: Start with Foundation 1 — dates and prices on the school page
items.priceNote: Per series — see the school page
items.why: The Bay Area Theatresports company has taught improv at Fort Mason for decades, and its six-level Foundation series is how a lot of people in San Francisco started. A weekly class with the same group for a series is half the appeal: you learn to say yes on stage, and you come out with a dozen new friends who also say yes to a drink afterwards.
items.hoursNote: Foundation 1 to 6 for adults, in person at Fort Mason and online

items.title: Letterpress at the San Francisco Center for the Book
items.cadence: Workshops most weeks · open print studio nights
items.times: Over 300 workshops a year; open print studio nights once you have taken the prerequisite class
items.firstStep: Book an introductory letterpress workshop — it unlocks studio time
items.priceNote: Per workshop · free events through the year
items.source: San Francisco Center for the Book
items.why: A print shop and bindery on Potrero Hill with more than three hundred workshops a year in letterpress, bookbinding and printmaking. The habit comes after the first class: that unlocks the open print studio nights, where experienced printers are on hand and you can rent a press for your own work.
items.hoursNote: Over 300 workshops a year; open print studio nights once you have taken the prerequisite class

items.title: Saturday tree plantings with Friends of the Urban Forest
items.times: Planting days generally run on Saturdays from 9am to 1pm, in a different neighbourhood each time
items.firstStep: Sign up for a planting on the volunteer page — no experience needed
items.area: A different San Francisco neighbourhood each week
items.why: Since 1981 this nonprofit has put close to a thousand street trees a year into San Francisco pavements, and it does it with volunteers on Saturday mornings. They cut the concrete, bring the trees and the tools; you dig beside the neighbours who asked for them. You do not need to live in the street, or in the city — and after a season you will have trees of your own dotted around town.
items.hoursNote: Planting days generally run on Saturdays from 9am to 1pm, in a different neighbourhood each time

items.title: Sing in Harmony, an open choir
items.times: Choir on Mondays 6pm to 8pm; chamber choir on Thursdays 7pm to 9pm
items.firstStep: No audition — come to a welcome session at the start of a season
items.area: Kanbar Performing Arts Center, 44 Page Street
items.why: A community choir with no audition, for anybody who wants to sing. Monday evenings in a performing arts centre off Market Street, with a smaller chamber choir on Thursdays once you want more. Each season opens with welcome sessions, so there is a clear moment to walk in rather than joining a room that already knows the songs.
items.hoursNote: Choir on Mondays 6pm to 8pm; chamber choir on Thursdays 7pm to 9pm

items.title: Cooking classes at 18 Reasons
items.times: A rolling calendar of hands-on classes: knife skills, baking, cuisines from around the world
items.firstStep: Book a single class from the calendar
items.priceNote: Per class · fees fund free cooking programmes
items.why: A nonprofit cooking school in the Mission where the paid evening classes — knife skills, bread, mushrooms, cuisines taught by cooks from all over — pay for free multi-week courses for low-income families. So your evening learning knife skills does some good. Book one, then another; people end up working through the calendar.
items.hoursNote: A rolling calendar of hands-on classes: knife skills, baking, cuisines from around the world

items.title: Book groups at Kepler's
items.times: Literary discussion groups through the month, hosted by staff and volunteers; the non-fiction group meets on the first Tuesday
items.firstStep: Free and drop-in — pick a group from the events page
items.area: Kepler's Books, 1010 El Camino Real, Menlo Park
items.why: The Peninsula's great independent bookshop runs eight to ten discussion groups a month, free and open to anybody who turns up. Some have been meeting for more than a decade; the non-fiction one votes on its books every three months. Choose the group whose next book you would have read anyway, and it becomes the monthly thing you never miss.
items.hoursNote: Literary discussion groups through the month, hosted by staff and volunteers; the non-fiction group meets on the first Tuesday

items.title: French at the Alliance Française de San Francisco
items.times: In-person and online courses at every level, in sessions through the year, with a cultural programme alongside
items.firstStep: Take the placement test, then sign up for the next session
items.why: A French language and cultural centre on Bush Street, teaching every level from absolute beginner up, in person and online. The classes are the habit; the cultural programme in the same building is what makes it feel like somewhere you belong rather than a course you are taking.
items.hoursNote: In-person and online courses at every level, in sessions through the year, with a cultural programme alongside
